text:
alex: Heads up — during tonight's nightly burn we saw 3 nodes flip to degraded within 30m. All from g2 racks in eq-12, pattern looks like brief PCIe link renegotiation + Xid 13.

sam: ugh. any dmesg snippet?

maria: pasted the short log below, grabbed from the first affected host (g2-rack12-07):

maria: ```
[ 2354.112345] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3a:00): 13, PID=8426 KERNEL_MODULE
[ 2354.112348] nvidia 0000:3a:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 2354.112350] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 00e0
[ 2354.112352] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer
[ 2354.112353] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: UESta=00000000, UEMsk=00000000, UESvrt=00000000
```

lee: that looks like lane training flaps (physical layer). Are these hosts on the same PSU/pdu chain or a riser batch?

alex: all three were on pdu-7, but different PSUs on the PDU. Risers came from the same supplier batch (R-2025-B).

sam: could be thermal or power rail ripple that only shows up during randomized memory sweeps. We should replicate deterministically: run a short randomized memtest + pci-stress for 45m.

maria: started a job: infra-bot queued: soak-mini-rand @g2-rack12-07,08,11 — duration 45m, workload: randmem + pcie-stress. Job id 4821.

infra-bot: "soak-mini-rand" job 4821 scheduled, ETA start 5m, nodes: g2-rack12-07,g2-rack12-08,g2-rack12-11. Notify @alex @sam @maria on complete.

lee: also collect:
- /sys/kernel/debug/pcie/* link_training logs
- output of `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 10`
- `lspci -vvv` for the slot to capture MaxLinkCap/CurrentLinkSpeed fields

alex: good call. maria can you add a cron that pulls `dmesg -T --ctime -l err,warn` every minute to a temp file during the run? Put it to /var/tmp/soak-logs/<job>/dmesg.log

maria: done. also enabled nvlink and pcie counters collection via telegraf plugin, metric names: pcie.link.retrain_count, pcie.aer.corrected_count.

sam: if we reproduce, next step is to swap riser on one node and re-run. If still flaky, escalate for vendor HW RMA.

alex: low-cost mitigation idea: route high-latency/large-batch shards away from these hosts (taint them for autoscaler) until cleared. Can someone add a temporary taint?

lee: adding a node-level taint: `kubectl taint nodes g2-rack12-07 hardware=flaky:NoSchedule` now.

infra-bot: Job 4821 started at 1765432300.

maria: first 12m of run — no new Xid, but pcie.link.retrain_count incremented twice on g2-rack12-07 (small spikes coincide with heavy cudaMemcpy patterns).

sam: that's a repro signal. schedule riser swap on 07 tomorrow morning, and run a 2h soak with slightly lower mem-intensity to see if it's workload-triggered or hardware.

alex: agreed. added TODOs to the incident doc:
- swap riser 07 tomorrow 09:00
- 2h reduced-intensity soak after swap
- capture BIOS event logs and seller-supplied riser serial numbers
- vendor support ticket if persists (attach job 4821 logs)

maria: exporting job 4821 logs now to s3://redwood-infra/soak-exports/4821.tar.gz and pinging @sam when upload completes.

infra-bot: Job 4821 completed at 1765432700. collected 84MB logs.

alex: thanks all. If swap doesn't fix it we'll plan an RMA and temporarily migrate workloads off pdu-7.

lee: nudge: I'll book a 30m window with facilities for physical access to rack 12 tomorrow morning.

sam: cool. add a small playbook entry for future: mini-randomized soak + taint + riser-swap -> RMA decision tree. Keep it lightweight so oncall can run it quickly. :white_check_mark:
